newsitem.title: INDIA: India Larsen to seek partners for Orissa projects.
newsitem.headline: India Larsen to seek partners for Orissa projects.

text.p: India's largest engineering and construction firm, Larsen & Toubro Ltd (L&T), said on Tuesday it planned to seek majority partners for steel and alumina plants it is building in the eastern state of Orissa.

"What we are doing is acting as developers for these two projects basically and then we will look for somebody to really take up these projects," L&T managing director Sudhakar Kulkarni told Reuters in an interview.

L&T is building a five-million-tonne-per-annum integrated steel plant to manufacture flat products in Orissa. Its alumina plant nearby, with a one-million-tonne-per-annum capacity is intended to convert bauxite to alumina for export.
L&T, which is also India's second largest cement maker, recently announced a net profit of 4.11 billion rupees for the year ended March 31, up from 3.89 billion in the previous year.
Kulkarni said L&T was primarily interested in the projects as an engineering contractor, which would supply equipment and construction services.
"We are now very clear... whether it is alumina or whether it is steel... we do not intend to make large investments in these projects," he added.
However, L&T was willing to take a minority stake in these ventures if that would help it get additional business.

"If for the purpose of tying up all these, the engineering, procurement, construction work etc, if we have to take a small equity in that we would, but otherwise we are not going to invest," Kulkarni said.
"An alumina project can require investments of the order of 30 billion rupees and a steel plant something like 80 billion rupees," he added.
"The company cannot go on making investments on this scale, but it has done a lot of work in these areas, and would very clearly like to derive a benefit of that."
Asked if any prospective partners had been identified, Kulkarni declined to name any suitors.
"We are not in a hurry. we would like to offer them to somebody. There can be many people who can be interested internationally. It's premature to name any."
L&T was merely following a growing international trend, Kulkarni said.

"This is commonly done all over the world. There are people who develop projects, and after a certain stage they get out of that project, and they keep whatever is their interest in that project and they invite others to take it up."
